chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, who said:

Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) liked grapes. So one day he was fasting, and when he broke his fast, the first thing that came was grapes. A mother of his child came to him with a cluster of grapes and placed it in front of him. A beggar came, so he gave it to him. His mother of child went to the beggar and bought it from him. Then she came with it and placed it in front of him. Another beggar came, so he gave it to him. The mother of the child did the same. Then she came with it and placed it in front of him. Another beggar came, so he gave it to him. The mother of the child did the same. When it was the fourth time, he ate it (peace be upon him).
ai.seo_question: What is the story of Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn and the grapes?
ai.summary: This narrative from *Al-Kafi* highlights the virtue of *sabr* (patience) and strategic generosity, where Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (Zayn al-Abidin) balanced his personal desire with the spiritual reward of charity. His mother of child’s clever intervention demonstrates the practical application of *fiqh* in daily life, ensuring that the act of giving did not become a burden while still fulfilling the obligation of *sadaqah*. This incident is often cited by Shia scholars to illustrate the balance between asceticism and enjoying lawful pleasures (*lutf*).
